items.title: Iran declares Strait of Hormuz open as Lebanon ceasefire begins
items.description: US President Donald Trump immediately welcomed the news from Tehran but went on to warn that the US blockade of Iran's ports would continue.

items.title: Live: Trump says US will go into Iran to remove 'nuclear dust'
items.description: Should a peace deal with Tehran be reached, the US president says he expects the US to work with Iran to recover what's left of its enriched uranium. Follow live.

items.title: The world faces a grim reality, even if Trump exists in a different one
items.description: The world is stuck watching a performative series of announcements about meetings that could, may, will happen, involving a president not dealing with the reality that he is in a weak and confused bargaining position.

items.title: Budget coincides with the thunderclap of history in flux — and hard choices
items.description: The budget's usual timing on the second Tuesday of May is an artifice of political convention. This year's edition just happens to be coinciding with the thunderclap of history in flux.

items.title: What crisis? Why stocks are ignoring the economy
items.description: The Australian Securities Exchange is within striking distance of new records as economists issue worst-case warnings of a close call for a global recession.

items.title: As Trump promotes a new ceasefire, many in Lebanon fear a bad deal
items.description: Donald Trump sold a ceasefire in Lebanon as a step towards peace. But that promise hinges on a condition that Lebanon may not be able to deliver.

items.title: Outcry over 'disturbing' video of off-duty police officer pinning 13yo girl on train
items.description: Video of an off-duty police officer restraining a 13yo girl on a Perth train has sparked accusations of excessive force.

items.title: Australia enters drone warfare era with Ghost Bat and Ghost Shark
items.description: Australia is on a push to keep pace with the rapid evolution of drone warfare, with an emphasis on locally produced Ghost Bat and Ghost Shark systems.

items.title: The Windsor playbook with a twist: Harry and Meghan's royal model
items.description: Mixing philanthropy, influencing and brand building, Harry and Meghan’s Australian tour revives a question Queen Elizabeth once shut down: can the 'half in, half out' royal life work?

items.title: Turbulence ahead as airfares fluctuate amid Middle East conflict
items.description: Australians are finding domestic flights for as little as $65 on some routes, while others are paying thousands to travel interstate as airlines quietly reshape the market in response to conflict in the Middle East.

items.title: Viva Energy says fire at Victorian refinery will not cause fuel supply issues
items.description: Despite the refinery running at reduced capacity following a fire, experts say the incident in Geelong this week should not significantly affect fuel prices.

items.title: Chinese device found in strategic waters near Bali identified
items.description: A large torpedo-shaped device discovered near an island in a strategically important strait between Bali and Lombok has been identified by defence analysts as a Chinese undersea monitoring system.

items.title: Labor considering ways to spare new homes from capital gains changes
items.description: The possible budget centrepiece is likely to be finalised much closer to the May deadline than usual this year given global uncertainty, but progress has been made in recent weeks.

items.title: The 'immense complexity' facing Ben Roberts-Smith's prosecutors
items.description: A legal expert says the criminal prosecution of former soldier Ben Roberts-Smith will test Australia's war crimes legal framework in ways never seen before, as the case moves toward a trial.

items.title: Popular outback motoring rally cancelled due to fuel crisis
items.description: As fuel becomes less available, Variety NSW is concerned its main fundraising event could harm the small communities it tries to support.

items.title: ABC 50/50 quiz: Test your knowledge of the Big Day Out, footy fairytales and the circles of hell
items.description: Every question has only two options: one is right, and the other is wrong. You have an even chance of guessing correctly each time.

items.title: It's generational warfare as millennials take on gen Z in Beef season 2
items.description: The dark comedy series returns with a biting look at generational conflict, starring Carey Mulligan and Oscar Isaac as a "combustible" middle-aged couple.

items.title: Aung San Suu Kyi to be freed sooner as Myanmar releases her ally from jail
items.description: Myanmar's ex-leader Aung San Suu Kyi has her prison sentence cut as thousands of prisoners are freed. Meanwhile, the UN reveals 2025 marked the deadliest year on record for Rohingya refugees fleeing Myanmar.

items.title: Daughter tells jury she saw mum crush drugs into lethal smoothie
items.description: The daughter of a Gold Coast woman accused of killing her son alleges she saw her mum use a hammer to crush up drugs before putting them into a lethal fruit smoothie.

items.title: 'Derek' the dingo a concern for some as he roams streets in outback town
items.description: An lone dingo, affectionately known as Derek, has been spotted in suburban streets, backyards and even in dog parks, raising some concern for Alice Springs residents.

items.title: Patients with little-known neurological condition wait years for diagnosis
items.description: People with functional neurological disorder say they experience misdiagnosis and struggles within the medical system.

items.title: Ben Roberts-Smith leaves jail after securing bail over alleged war crimes
items.description: Ben Roberts-Smith was granted bail after spending a week in custody over alleged war crime of murder offences.

items.title: AI Val Kilmer branded 'terrifying', but filmmakers say movie is ethical
items.description: A trailer for a film with an AI-generated character in the likeness of the late Val Kilmer has been slammed by social media users, but the filmmakers are defending their work.

items.title: Young people leaving Sydney 'en masse' over housing affordability
items.description: Productivity Commissioner Danielle Wood says Australia will not meet the federal government's 1.2 million new home target, as residential construction rates fall.

items.title: 'Completely broken': Parents share anguish after fatal police collision
items.description: The parents of 16-year-old Jai Kalani Wright, who died after colliding with a police car, share their emotional testimonies in court as the sentencing hearing begins.
